title: C# projects cannot be exported to the web
description: Godot 4 cannot load the .NET runtime into its prebuilt WASM, so a C#/.NET project has no web export at all (Godot 3 Mono could).
evidence_issues: #70796 (open/reopened, 103 reactions, 116 comments; locked 2026-06-19 by akien-mga: "The foundation is evaluating solutions for C# web support") | PR #106125 "[.NET] Add web export support" (open draft, 451 reactions) | raulsntos in #70796 (2025-01-11): dotnet/runtime#75257 "seems to be the main blocker"
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "Projects written in C# using Godot 4 currently cannot be exported to the web platform. To use C# on the web platform, consider Godot 3 instead." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/export/exporting_for_web.html "Note that GDExtensions still need to be specifically compiled for the web platform to work. Like thread support, enabling this feature requires the use of cross-origin isolation headers."
evidence_source: unverified (the blocker is loading the .NET WASM runtime, outside modules/mono)
frequency: 2nd most-reacted topic:dotnet issue (GraphQL search label:topic:dotnet sort:reactions-desc); draft PR has 451 reactions; 6 issues mention "70796" (GraphQL issue search)
status: open (no C# web export in 4.x; draft PR #106125)
fix_reason: Absent without .NET; analog: Petrichor's runtime must target WASM - compiled into export templates as a module it needs nothing extra, as a GDExtension it works only with Extensions Support (dlink) templates and COOP/COEP headers.

title: Mobile C# export is experimental; NuGet native libraries not packaged
description: C# export to Android/iOS arrived only in 4.2 and is still experimental; native libraries shipped in NuGet packages are not copied into Android builds, so they fail at runtime with DllNotFoundException.
evidence_issues: #68153 Add C# support for Android in Godot 4.x (closed completed, milestone 4.2, 234 reactions, 26 comments) | #97859 Android build doesn't include native libraries from NuGet packages (open, 8 reactions, 15 comments; still reported on 4.5 on 2025-11-01) | #84559 C# Android SSL crash using HttpClient (closed 2024-09-17, 8 reactions, 25 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/index.html "Android support is currently experimental." | "iOS support is currently experimental and has a few limitations." | "Exporting to iOS can only be done from a macOS device."
evidence_source: unverified
frequency: #68153 is the most-reacted topic:dotnet issue overall (234, GraphQL search sorted by reactions)
fix_reason: NuGet/.NET packaging is .NET-specific; analog: any Petrichor native dependency must be packaged per platform by its own export plugin (EditorExportPlugin is a bound, extensible class), no module needed.

title: Separate .NET editor build, external SDK and MSBuild project files
description: C# needs a different Godot binary plus a separately installed .NET SDK of a pinned major version, and builds through csproj/MSBuild, so SDK/IDE upgrades, project renames and CI exports can break outside Godot's control.
evidence_issues: #68652 cannot create or build C# solution after Visual Studio 17.4 / .NET 7 upgrade (closed, 5 reactions, 8 comments) | #94957 CLI export returns exit code 0 when the C# build failed (open, 2 reactions, 9 comments) | #27030 changing project name breaks all C# scripts (closed 2022-08-22, fixed by #64089 in 4.0 and #64460 in 3.6; 15 reactions, 17 comments; cross-referenced by #47528 #46290 #60471 #15624)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/index.html "The standard Godot executable does not contain C# support out of the box." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "Godot does not bundle the tools required to build and compile games, such as MSBuild and the C# compiler. These are included in the .NET SDK, and need to be installed separately." | "Godot 4.8 requires .NET 10 or later."
evidence_source: modules/mono/utils/path_utils.cpp:232-235 (assembly name falls back to application/config/name when dotnet/project/assembly_name is empty)
frequency: low reactions per issue but recurring: 4 rename duplicates cross-referenced from #27030; build-related titles are common (232 topic:dotnet issues with "build" in the title, GraphQL count, not all relevant)
fix_reason: A compiler shipped inside the engine binary (module or GDExtension) needs no external SDK, project file or second editor build; keeping project identity out of user-editable names is a toolchain choice.

title: Editor sees new exports, signals and tool changes only after a build
description: The inspector, signal list and tool scripts reflect the last compiled assembly, not the source, so a saved .cs edit changes nothing in the editor until Build is pressed (and some registrations needed an editor restart).
example: add [Export] public int Hp { get; set; } -> absent from the Inspector until Build
evidence_issues: #12518 new export variables won't show until restart (closed 2018-08-05, 10 reactions, 43 comments) | #116169 [GlobalClass] not registered until editor restart when file created externally (closed 2026-03-19 by #117617, milestone 4.7; 12 reactions) | godot-proposals#2920 Auto (re)build project when C# script changes (open, 33 reactions) | godot-proposals#849 Implement background building of project solution (open, 15 reactions)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "You need to (re)build the project assemblies whenever you want to see new exported variables or signals in the editor." | "You will also need to rebuild the project assemblies to apply changes in "tool" scripts." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_exports.html "after building the current project it will be visible in the property editor."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotPlugins/Main.cs:156 (script types are discovered by scanning the loaded compiled project assembly, not the source)
frequency: 48 reactions on the two auto-build proposals; shown as a warning box in the C# basics page
status: by-design (manual Build button); auto-build proposals open
fix_reason: If the language front end parses source on save, the editor can show declarations without a build step; ScriptExtension update_exports/_get_script_property_list/reload are GDExtension virtuals (core/object/script_language_extension.h:79,176,188).

title: Scenes opened against a stale or unbuilt assembly lose exported values
description: After pulling teammates' changes, scenes load before the new assembly is built; properties the old assembly does not declare are dropped and re-saved, silently losing exported node references and data.
evidence_issues: #86193 4.2 .NET scene keeps losing exported references between commits from different users (open, 13 reactions, 1 comment) | #90755 Godot should pre-compile C# project on load to prevent scene data loss with collaborative workflow (open, 8 reactions, 8 comments)
evidence_source: core/object/object.cpp:1066-1071 (a script that cannot instantiate gets a placeholder instance in the editor) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:819-826 (placeholder keeps unknown properties via fallback only during a failed reload) | exact drop path unverified
frequency: 21 reactions over 2 open issues; #90755 comment (2024-08-07): "Almost every push requires the people working on the project to get in vc and explain to one another how to setup the exports"
fix_reason: Removable when declarations come from source parsed at load time instead of a build artifact; a placeholder that keeps unknown properties (is_placeholder_fallback_enabled is a ScriptExtension virtual, script_language_extension.h:218) prevents silent drops.

title: Assembly unloading fails on rebuild; C# unusable until editor restart
description: Editor rebuilds need the collectible AssemblyLoadContext to unload; any strong GC handle, running thread, captured delegate or incompatible library (e.g. Newtonsoft.Json) blocks it, and then all C# scripts stay unavailable until restart.
example: [Tool] class doing GCHandle.Alloc(this) in _Ready -> ".NET: Failed to unload assemblies"
evidence_issues: #78513 tracker (open, 95 reactions, 194 comments; body: "After unloading has failed, C# scripts will be unavailable until the editor is restarted") | #81903 capturing a variable in a Callable prevents assembly unloading (closed 2024-04-05 by #83217, milestone 4.3; 15 reactions) | #79519 generic script registration errors in ScriptManagerBridge (closed, 27 reactions, 28 comments) | #102484 Failed to unload with TweenMethod/TweenCallback in tool script (closed) | #110784 generic and non-generic classes with same name (open, 3 reactions)
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotPlugins/Main.cs:254-277 (forced GC loop gives up after 1000 ms: "Possible causes: Strong GC handles, running threads, etc.") | modules/mono/mono_gd/gd_mono.cpp:810-813 (prints the #78513 link and counts a failure) | gd_mono.cpp:795 ("Giving up on assembly reloading. Please restart the editor if unloading was failing.")
frequency: 3rd most-reacted topic:dotnet issue; the engine error message links straight to #78513; 16 issues mention "78513" (GraphQL issue search)
status: open (tracker; individual causes fixed case by case)
fix_reason: Collectible-ALC unloading is .NET-specific; analog: Petrichor reload must not depend on unloading a native library - VM-owned code objects can be swapped via ScriptLanguageExtension _reload_scripts/_reload_tool_script (script_language_extension.h:686,690), and the language can disallow untracked global roots.

title: Reload resets state that is not a writable Variant-compatible member
description: On rebuild each instance is serialized and restored, but only non-static, read-write, Variant-compatible fields/properties survive; readonly fields, init-only properties, statics, List<T>/plain C# objects and lambdas are reset, and IDE (.NET) hot reload is unsupported.
example: private List<int> _cache = new(); // empty again after every rebuild in a [Tool] script
evidence_issues: #76898 C# collection content gets lost on build (open, 3 reactions) | #67719 .NET 6 hot reload throws exceptions (open, 10 reactions, 6 comments) | #37812 base class members reset to defaults if derived class has [Tool] (closed 2021-12-28 by #56299, milestone 4.0; 9 reactions, 22 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "State is currently not saved and restored when hot-reloading, with the exception of exported variables."
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptSerializationGenerator.cs:117-135 (saves only non-static, read-write, Godot-compatible members; TODO says read-only ones are not restored; broader than the docs' 'exported only') | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:753-775 (per-instance state backup before reload)
frequency: low reactions; listed by the docs among "the most important issues"
fix_reason: Petrichor can define which state survives reload (e.g. all fields of statically known types, with explicit migration hooks) and implement it in its own _reload_scripts; .NET IDE hot reload is N/A.

title: += signal handlers are not disconnected when the receiver is freed
description: A lambda that captures a variable has a closure object as Delegate.Target, so its Callable carries no receiver ObjectID; custom [Signal] events live in a managed backing delegate on the emitter; neither is removed when the receiver dies, giving ObjectDisposedException or leaks.
example: timer.Timeout += () => { x++; GD.Print(Name); }; Free(); // next tick: ObjectDisposedException
evidence_issues: #70414 (open, confirmed, 40 reactions, 20 comments) | #82346 autoload signal connected through C# delegate does not disconnect when receiver is freed (closed not_planned, 2 reactions) | #66319 signal connected through C# delegate does not disconnect (closed 2022)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_signals.html "When a signal receiver is freed while the signal emitter is still alive, in some cases automatic disconnection won't happen: - The signal is connected to a lambda expression that captures a variable. - The signal is a custom signal."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Callable.cs:74 (_target = @delegate?.Target as GodotObject) | modules/mono/managed_callable.cpp:81-86 (without a target the callable's object is the shared middleman, never freed with the receiver) | modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/ScriptSignalsGenerator.cs:303-308 (custom signal event add/remove only touch a managed backing_ delegate)
frequency: 9th most-reacted topic:dotnet issue (40); 7 issues mention "70414" (GraphQL issue search); the signals page devotes a section to it
fix_reason: Petrichor can define closures and method references as bound to their creating object and create the CallableCustom with that object_id (GDExtensionCallableCustomInfo2.object_id, core/extension/gdextension_interface.json:2460-2474), routing custom signals through engine connections.

title: Managed reference outlives the freed object; Dispose() does not free
description: After Free()/QueueFree() the C# reference stays non-null and any use throws ObjectDisposedException, so null checks lie and IsInstanceValid is needed; conversely Dispose() on a non-RefCounted object only drops the wrapper (and detaches the C# script) and leaks the native object.
example: tree.CreateItem(root).Dispose(); // TreeItem leaks and can no longer be Free()d (#86926)
evidence_issues: #86926 C# .Dispose() should free the object from memory (open, 13 reactions, 14 comments) | #107579 Dispose() causes memory leaks (open, 3 reactions, 13 comments; flagged as probable duplicate of #86926) | #99152 "Cannot access a disposed object" with exported node and scene inheritance (closed duplicate, 4 reactions) | #71032 ObjectDisposedException on internal nodes after reloading a scene (closed not_planned)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_signals.html "If you encounter a System.ObjectDisposedException while handling a signal, you might be missing a signal disconnection." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_differences.html maps is_instance_valid(obj) to GodotObject.IsInstanceValid(obj)
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/GodotObject.base.cs:93 (every native call throws ObjectDisposedException once NativePtr is zero) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:1232-1235 (on native free the wrapper's NativePtr is zeroed; the wrapper stays alive) | modules/mono/glue/runtime_interop.cpp:140-166 (Dispose of a non-RefCounted object releases the GC handle and calls set_script_instance(nullptr); the Object is not deleted)
frequency: 26 topic:dotnet issues match "ObjectDisposedException" (GraphQL search); forum threads e.g. https://forum.godotengine.org/t/c-cannot-access-a-disposed-object/24885 | https://forum.godotengine.org/t/how-to-tell-if-a-node3d-is-disposed-cannot-access-a-disposed-object-object-name-godot-node3d/46933 | https://forum.godotengine.org/t/random-problem-of-object-disposed/121671
fix_reason: Petrichor can give freed-object references a defined, checkable state (e.g. compare equal to null) and a single destroy verb; liveness is queryable through object_get_instance_from_id in the GDExtension interface (gdextension_interface.json:7960).

title: Engine references released by the .NET GC: late, off-thread and racy
description: When only C# holds a RefCounted, release waits for a GC finalizer on another thread; the resource cache can resurrect a Resource whose wrapper was already collected, losing the GC handle and crashing with FATAL "gchandle.is_released()".
evidence_issues: #83762 random crash on scene change, Condition "gchandle.is_released()" is true (open, 9 reactions, 39 comments; reproduced on master by akien-mga 2025-05-13; still on 4.7.2 per 2026-10-07 comment) | #112067 intermittent "Handle is not initialized" instantiating a PackedScene referencing a cached CompressedTexture2D (open, 7 reactions, 7 comments) | #104263 RenderingDevice resources disposed on the wrong thread (closed, 4 reactions, 9 comments)
evidence_docs: - (maintainer raulsntos in #104263, 2025-06-24: "finalizers are executed on a different thread from the rendering thread, so if these resources must be freed on the rendering thread you'll need to properly dispose them")
evidence_source: modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:1296-1300 (when the engine drops its last reference the managed wrapper "takes responsibility of deleting the owner when GCed") | csharp_script.cpp:1990-2000 (refcount_incremented clears the handle and returns if the target was already collected) | csharp_script.cpp:1916 (CRASH_COND(gchandle.is_released()) in mono_object_disposed_baseref) | modules/mono/glue/runtime_interop.cpp:168-201 (finalizer path, p_is_finalizer)
frequency: #83762: 39 comments over 3 years; root cause traced by paulloz (2026-08) to resource-cache resurrection; 4 issues mention "83762" (GraphQL issue search)
fix_reason: The race needs a second tracing heap; Petrichor avoids it by holding engine objects through the engine's own refcount (deterministic, on the releasing thread) rather than GC finalizers, using instance-binding callbacks from the GDExtension interface for any wrapper cache.

title: Struct-typed properties return copies (CS1612)
description: Vector2/Transform3D etc. are C# structs, so Position.X = 5 is a compile error and modifying a local copy without reassigning it silently does nothing; each read and write is a separate interop call.
example: Position.X = 100f; // CS1612 -> var p = Position; p.X = 100f; Position = p;
evidence_issues: - (no engine issue; treated as normal C# behaviour)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "Structs (in this example, a Vector2) in C# are copied on assignment, meaning that when you retrieve such an object from a property or an indexer, you get a copy of it, not the object itself. Modifying said copy without reassigning it afterwards won't achieve anything."
evidence_source: unverified (C# language rule; no engine code involved)
frequency: the only item in the C# basics "Common pitfalls" section; forum threads https://forum.godotengine.org/t/unable-to-solve-error-with-c/50270 (2024-03, Node3D.Transform) | https://forum.godotengine.org/t/cant-modify-globalposition-on-a-node2d-inheriter-in-c/127324 (2025-11, GlobalPosition)
fix_reason: The language can define obj.prop.x = v as get-modify-set along the property chain (GDScript accepts position.x = 100), keeping value semantics without the trap.

title: Packed arrays are marshalled as fresh System.Array copies
description: PackedVector2Array etc. map to T[]; every property read copies the whole native buffer into a new managed array, so indexed writes like line.Points[0] = v compile but change nothing, and indexing a property in a loop is O(n) per access.
evidence_issues: godot-proposals#7842 Expose a zero allocation API to Godot C# bindings (open, 497 reactions, 97 comments; "GC is allocated on return" | "Memory is copied to Godot native formats every time there is a call")
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_collections.html "In C#, packed arrays are replaced by System.Array" | class reference (doc/classes/PackedByteArray.xml:9, also applies to GDScript): "In these cases the returned packed array is a copy, and changing it will not affect the original value."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/Marshaling.cs:437-446 (allocates a new byte[] and copies the native buffer on every conversion)
frequency: #7842 has 497 reactions (allocation and copy concerns); forum https://forum.godotengine.org/t/cannot-update-individual-points-of-line2d-in-c/8881 (2021)
fix_reason: Copy-on-read of packed-array properties is core behaviour, but Petrichor can expose packed arrays as engine COW values without conversion and define obj.prop[i] = v as write-back or reject it at compile time.

title: Two collection families; only Godot collections cross the boundary
description: Engine APIs and [Export] accept only Variant-compatible Godot.Collections.Array/Dictionary (or T[] for packed arrays); .NET List/Dictionary cannot be exported, converting copies every element, and picking the wrong family for an untyped Array parameter fails silently.
example: [Export] List<string> Names; // GD0102: The type of the exported member is not supported
evidence_issues: #70298 C# Export on List not possible anymore (open, 38 reactions, 7 comments) | #65937 ArrayMesh.AddSurfaceFromArrays doesn't work with Godot.Collections.Array as vertex array (closed, 4 reactions; needs Vector3[] instead) | #95358 cannot export C# array of Vector2I/Vector3I/Vector4I (open, 1 reaction, 7 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_collections.html "every operation on a Godot collection requires marshaling which can be expensive especially inside a loop." | "this conversion requires marshaling every element in the collection and copies it to a new collection so it can be expensive." | https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_exports.html "Exporting can only be done with Variant-compatible types."
evidence_source: modules/mono/editor/Godot.NET.Sdk/Godot.SourceGenerators/Common.cs:50-58 (GD0102 error for non-Variant-compatible exported member types)
frequency: #70298: 38 reactions (tied 10th most-reacted topic:dotnet issue, GraphQL search sorted by reactions)
status: by-design (.NET collection export dropped in the .NET 6 move, PR #64089, per raulsntos in #70298)
fix_reason: A language whose built-in arrays and dictionaries are the engine's (typed) Array/Dictionary/Packed*Array has one family, so there is no conversion or export gap.

title: Variant-to-type conversions silently coerce or default
description: Casting a Variant to a C# type does not check the Variant type: "42a" becomes 42, unrelated types become 0/default, and int64 is truncated to int, so marshalling mistakes surface as wrong values instead of errors.
evidence_issues: - (no dedicated issue found: GraphQL search label:topic:dotnet "Variant conversion As<" gave no relevant hit)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_variant.html "If the Variant type doesn't match the conversion target type, the consequences vary depending on the source and target values." | "For example, the string "42a" may be converted to the integer 42." | "The default value of the target type may be returned."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/VariantUtils.cs:370-373 (non-Int variants go through godotsharp_variant_as_int, then an unchecked (int) cast) | core/variant/variant.h:342-357 (_to_int: NIL->0, STRING->to_int(), any other type->0)
frequency: docs-only signal
fix_reason: Petrichor can make Variant->T conversions checked (test variant_get_type, gdextension_interface.json:5001, before converting) and reserve lossy coercion for explicit functions.

title: Hidden per-call allocations cause GC frame spikes
description: Passing a string where a StringName/NodePath is expected allocates a finalizable wrapper plus a native StringName on every call, and APIs returning Godot collections allocate too; one such call per frame is enough for visible GC stutter.
evidence_issues: #105750 Stutters/frame spikes when using C# (open, 20 reactions, 20 comments; MRP: one StringName construction or GetNodesInGroup per frame) | godot-proposals#7842 zero allocation API (open, 497 reactions) | godot-proposals#15089 cache StringName and NodePath conversions in C# (open, 24 reactions) | #104180 excessive StringName allocation when subclassing AnimationTree (closed, 3 reactions)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "The implicit conversion from string to NodePath or StringName incur both the native interop and marshalling costs as the string has to be marshalled and passed to the respective native constructor." | "Prefer using the exposed StringName in the PropertyName, MethodName and SignalName to avoid extra StringName allocations"
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/StringName.cs:81 (implicit operator StringName(string from) => new StringName(from)) | StringName.cs:68-75 (creates a native StringName and registers the object in DisposablesTracker) | StringName.cs:22-25 (finalizer) | NodePath.cs:135 (same for NodePath)
frequency: #7842 497 reactions; #105750 20 reactions; #15089 24 reactions
status: open (workaround: cache StringName, use generated SignalName/MethodName)
fix_reason: Petrichor can type such parameters as StringName, intern string literals at compile time and warn on runtime String->StringName conversions in hot paths; without a tracing GC there is no pause to trigger.

title: Engine-to-script callbacks slow with many scripted nodes
description: Every engine call into a C# script (_Process, notifications, even for empty scripts) went through name-matching dispatch in InvokeGodotClassMethod, so thousands of scripted nodes cost far more than the script bodies.
example: 300 Buttons with an empty C# script: 1000 -> 400 FPS (#115960)
evidence_issues: #89217 unexpected C# performance loss on simple scripts (closed 2026-09-26 by PR #116300 "C#: Optimize C++ to .NET calls with delegate* and hash map lookup", milestone 4.8; 36 reactions, 19 comments) | #98175 terrible performance with several scripted nodes (closed not_planned, consolidated into #89217; 14 reactions) | #115960 performance loss with empty C# script due to frequent string equality check (closed 2026-10-14, 5 reactions) | #96435 C# about 5x slower in Godot than in a console app (open, reopened, 2 reactions, 16 comments)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "Most properties of Godot C# objects that are based on GodotObject (e.g. any Node like Control or Node3D like Camera3D) require native (interop) calls as they talk to Godot's C++ core."
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/CSharpInstanceBridge.cs:10-25 (each ScriptInstance call enters managed code and dispatches by StringName through InvokeGodotClassMethod)
frequency: 55 reactions across #89217/#98175/#115960; fix PR #116300 has 38 reactions
status: fixed (PR #116300, 4.8) for the dispatch path; #96435 open
fix_reason: Petrichor implements the script-instance call callback itself (it receives the method StringName), so it can resolve methods once per class and dispatch by hashed StringName.

title: Unhandled exceptions are logged and the game keeps running
description: Exceptions escaping a C# callback are caught by the bridge, printed (sent to the debugger as an error, not a break) and the call just returns; Godot 3's unhandled-exception policy and GD.UnhandledException are gone, so a game can run on in a corrupted state.
example: public override void _Process(double d) { throw new Exception(); } // error printed every frame, game continues
evidence_issues: #73515 options for dealing with unhandled C# exceptions present in Godot 3 are missing in Godot 4 (open, confirmed, 20 reactions, 13 comments) | #28259 prevent C# exceptions from terminating the game (closed 2019-12-13, 7 reactions; a 2023 comment asks whether configurable handling was removed in 4.x) | #67451 4.0 C# error messages needlessly obfuscated (closed 2023-01-27 by #71943, milestone 4.0; 13 reactions)
evidence_docs: - (no statement on exception policy in the C# docs pages)
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/CSharpInstanceBridge.cs:39-43 (catch-all: log and return false) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/ExceptionUtils.cs:108-119 (send to debugger or PushError) | modules/mono/glue/runtime_interop.cpp:100-105 (send_error only, no debug break) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/GodotUnhandledExceptionEvent.cs:16-24 (AppDomain handler installed only in debug builds)
frequency: #73515 20 reactions
fix_reason: Petrichor defines runtime-error semantics (abort the current call or coroutine, configurable policy) and can break into the editor debugger via EngineDebugger.script_debug (bound at core/core_bind.cpp:2349), as GDScript does.

title: async/await and threads: lost exceptions, thread hops, loader deadlocks
description: Exceptions in fire-and-forget async Task methods are never reported; continuations return to the main thread only through a frame-polled SynchronizationContext, so Task.Run/ConfigureAwait(false) silently move scene access to pool threads; worker-thread loading of C# scripts also deadlocked.
example: _ = LoadAsync(); // an exception inside LoadAsync is never printed
evidence_issues: #25015 no errors reported for async functions, game continues (open, 3.x) | #85234 async Task no print error (closed 2023-11-22: .NET by-design) | #90300 error flood when GodotObject.Set is called from a C# thread (open, 5 reactions) | #79164 Node3D Position read in a Thread returns zero (closed) | #99128 ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest stuck at 0.5 (closed 2025-07-09 by #99539 in 4.4 and #99798 in 4.5; 18 reactions, 37 comments) | #104196 LoadThreadedRequest never finishes (closed 2025-10-22, 13 reactions, 12 comments)

title: In the editor, non-[Tool] scripted objects are only their native base type
description: Non-tool scripts get placeholder instances in the editor, so [Tool] code and editor plugins see such objects as plain Node/Resource; casts and typed [Export] setters throw InvalidCastException, pushing users to mark every class [Tool].
example: [Tool] partial class A : Resource { [Export] Blackboard B { get; set; } } // assigning a non-tool Blackboard -> InvalidCastException (#85459)
evidence_issues: #36395 Mono editor plugins can't cast non-tool C# types (open, 24 reactions, 22 comments; "The exact same structure and code in Gdscript works as intended") | #85459 InvalidCastException: Unable to cast 'Godot.Resource' to 'Blackboard' (open, 19 reactions, 20 comments; workaround quoted there: "all the classes involved in the hierarchy have to be [Tool] scripts")
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/plugins/running_code_in_the_editor.html "Code from other nodes doesn't run in the editor. Your access to other nodes is limited. You can access the tree and nodes, and their default properties, but you can't access user variables." | "any other GDScript that your tool script uses must also be a tool"
evidence_source: core/object/object.cpp:1066-1071 (a script that cannot instantiate gets placeholder_instance_create in the editor) | modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp:2540-2554 (can_instantiate is false for non-tool scripts while scripting is disabled in the editor)
frequency: 43 reactions over the two open issues; #85459 comment (2026-03-07): "I'm making all my scripts [Tool] and [GlobalClass] without thinking too much about it"
fix_reason: The placeholder rule is engine-wide (GDScript has it too), but Petrichor's casts and type tests can consult Object.get_script() inheritance, which placeholders keep, and its placeholder (via _placeholder_instance_create) can hold typed property values, so no engine change is needed.

title: Scripts must live in the single main project assembly
description: Script classes are discovered only in the main project assembly, so scripts in an extra csproj, a referenced DLL/NuGet package or another project's export cannot be attached ("associated class could not be found"), which rules out binary C# add-ons.
evidence_issues: #75352 loading/assigning a script exported from another project fails (open, confirmed, 11 reactions, 30 comments) | #77675 scripts cannot be loaded from additional C# projects (closed not_planned, consolidated into #75352; 14 reactions) | #95036 [GlobalClass] inheriting from a base class in another assembly not listed in Create New Node (open, 6 reactions) | #39921 unable to load C# add-on script (open, 16 reactions, 29 comments; causes vary)
evidence_docs: - (RedworkDE in #77675: "currently scripts are fundamentally only looked up in the main assembly")
evidence_source: modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotPlugins/Main.cs:156 (LookupScriptsInAssembly is called only for the project assembly) | modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:302-313 (types registered by their ScriptPathAttribute res:// path)
frequency: 47 reactions over 4 issues
fix_reason: Assembly scoping is .NET-specific; analog: Petrichor libraries and add-ons need a packaging and lookup scheme fixed by the toolchain (scripts are resources addressed by path, so source add-ons work by default).

title: Weak built-in editor and IDE plumbing for C#
description: Godot's script editor offers no C# completion and mis-highlights new C# files, so work moves to an external IDE, where GD.Print/Debug.WriteLine/Debug.Assert do not reach Visual Studio's output and the built-in editor's buffer could overwrite external edits.
evidence_issues: #73438 new C# scripts use incorrect syntax highlighting (open, confirmed, 9 reactions, 18 comments) | godot-proposals#712 built-in script editor and autocompletion for C# (open, 36 reactions) | #108965 missing GD.Print/Debug.WriteLine/Debug.Assert output in Visual Studio (open, 14 reactions) | godot-proposals#8648 GD.Print logs in Visual Studio Output tab (open, 27 reactions) | #50163 C# scripts get reset/reverted by Godot (closed 2024-01-29 by #82113, milestone 4.3; 8 reactions, 42 comments; further reports to 2024-12)
evidence_docs: https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html "C# support in Godot's built-in script editor is minimal. Consider using an external IDE or editor"
evidence_source: modules/mono has no complete_code/lookup_code override (grep count 0), so core/object/editor_language.h:123 default (complete_code returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE) applies
frequency: 63 reactions on the two proposals plus 31 on the three issues
fix_reason: ScriptLanguageExtension exposes _validate, _complete_code and _lookup_code (core/object/script_language_extension.h:393,493,533), so a new language can ship first-class built-in editing and print through the engine's own output.
